newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on stable peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat on stable peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged at 18.20 percent on Monday after trading within a narrow range due to a stable peso, dealers said.
Dealers added that overnight rates traded at an average rate of 18 percent.
"The market was very calm with rates stable. The stable peso bolstered the downward trend in rates," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 0.2 of a centavo softer at 7.7520/7.7540 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended down 20 basis points at 19.40 percent.
Traders said inflation figures also fueled forecasts that primary rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes could fall by 100 basis points at Tuesday's central bank auction.
Banco de Mexico announced in late trade the Consumer Price Index increased by 0.89 percent during the first half of February, compared to 2.57 percent.
A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms showed they had expected consumer prices to gain by 0.88 percent for February 1-15.
"A stable peso and positive news on the economic front continue to pave the way for cuts in primary rates," a trader said, who predicted a floor rate for 28-day Cetes at 18.50 percent.
Banco de Mexico assigned 28-day Cetes at 19.46 percent at last week's auction.
The central bank offset surplus liquidity in the system by draining 2.619 billion pesos through four auctions.
Liquidity of 219 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
